title: Some Say Marry Money But My Brother Says Big Brains Matter More

sections.overview: Classifies each of the twelve cranial nerves as Sensory, Motor, or Both so the modality predicts the deficit pattern and guides the exam.

sections.collegeNotes:
Classifies each of the twelve cranial nerves as Sensory, Motor, or Both so the modality predicts the deficit pattern and guides the exam.

### Some — Sensory — Olfactory (CN I)

Sensory

CN I is purely sensory (olfaction) with no motor component.

**Physiology.** Olfaction only reports to the brain; it moves nothing, so the nerve is purely afferent.

### Say — Sensory — Optic (CN II)

Sensory

CN II is purely sensory (vision), a direct CNS tract with no motor fibers.

**Physiology.** Vision is a pure input channel, making the optic nerve exclusively afferent.

### Marry — Motor — Oculomotor (CN III)

Motor

CN III is predominantly motor (extraocular muscles + levator palpebrae); its parasympathetic pupil-constricting fibers are an autonomic bonus, not a sensory function.

**Physiology.** Its main job is moving muscles, so it is grouped as Motor.

### Money — Motor — Trochlear (CN IV)

Motor

CN IV is purely motor, supplying only the superior oblique muscle.

**Physiology.** One muscle, no sensation — a single-purpose motor nerve.

### But — Both — Trigeminal (CN V)

Both

CN V is the classic mixed nerve: sensory to the face (V1/V2/V3) and motor to the muscles of mastication.

**Physiology.** It senses the face and mouth while driving the jaw, so it carries both afferent and efferent fibers.

### My — Motor — Abducens (CN VI)

Motor

CN VI is purely motor, supplying only the lateral rectus muscle.

**Physiology.** One muscle, one direction, motor only.

### Brother — Both — Facial (CN VII)

Both

CN VII is mixed: motor to facial expression, sensory (taste, anterior two-thirds of tongue), plus parasympathetic output to lacrimal and salivary glands.

**Physiology.** It moves the face while sensing taste and protecting the eye, so it carries both directions.

### Says — Sensory — Vestibulocochlear (CN VIII)

Sensory

CN VIII is purely sensory: hearing (cochlear) and balance (vestibular), with no motor component.

**Physiology.** Hearing and equilibrium are pure inputs, so the nerve is exclusively afferent.

### Big — Both — Glossopharyngeal (CN IX)

Both

CN IX is mixed: sensory/taste to the posterior tongue and pharynx, motor to the stylopharyngeus, and the afferent limb of the gag reflex.

**Physiology.** It senses the throat to trigger swallowing while helping move it, so it needs both directions.

### Brains — Both — Vagus (CN X)

Both

CN X is mixed: sensory to pharynx/larynx/viscera, motor to pharynx/larynx, plus extensive parasympathetic output to heart, lungs, and gut.

**Physiology.** The vagus senses organ state and commands them, making it the body's largest mixed nerve.

### Matter — Motor — Accessory (CN XI)

Motor

CN XI is purely motor, supplying the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.

**Physiology.** Movement-only, so it is classified Motor.

### More — Motor — Hypoglossal (CN XII)

Motor

CN XII is purely motor, supplying the muscles of the tongue.

**Physiology.** The tongue is all muscle movement, so the nerve is Motor.

sections.eli10:
A sentence that tells you, for each of the twelve brain wires, whether it's a 'feeling-in' wire (Sensory), an 'orders-out' wire (Motor), or a 'both-ways' wire (Both).

**Some — Sensory — Olfactory (CN I).** Smell is a one-way trip into the brain: chemicals in the air travel up the nose and report back, so this wire only carries 'news in.'

**Say — Sensory — Optic (CN II).** Seeing is information going in — light enters the eye and the picture is delivered to the brain, a one-way input road.

**Marry — Motor — Oculomotor (CN III).** The Oculomotor nerve is the eye's mover — it pulls the eye up, down, and inward and lifts the eyelid, sending orders out to muscles.

**Money — Motor — Trochlear (CN IV).** The Trochlear nerve moves one muscle — the one that tips the eye down and in — a clean, single-purpose orders-out wire.

**But — Both — Trigeminal (CN V).** The Trigeminal nerve does two jobs at once: it feels the whole face (sensory) AND powers the chewing muscles (motor) — a two-way street.

**My — Motor — Abducens (CN VI).** The Abducens nerve moves one muscle — the one that slides the eye sideways toward the ear — a one-way orders-out wire.

**Brother — Both — Facial (CN VII).** The Facial nerve does two jobs: it moves the face to smile and frown (motor) AND tastes the front of the tongue and runs tears (sensory) — a two-way street.

**Says — Sensory — Vestibulocochlear (CN VIII).** 'Says' reminds you of sound: hearing is information going in, along with the balance bubble — both are inputs, so this wire is one-way in.

**Big — Both — Glossopharyngeal (CN IX).** The Glossopharyngeal nerve feels the back of the throat and tastes bitter things (sensory) AND helps start the swallow (motor) — a two-way street.

**Brains — Both — Vagus (CN X).** The Vagus is the busiest two-way street: it feels the throat and organs AND runs the voice, swallow, and calm-down controls — feeling in and orders out.

**Matter — Motor — Accessory (CN XI).** The Accessory nerve moves two big muscles — shrug the shoulder and turn the head — a clean orders-out wire.

**More — Motor — Hypoglossal (CN XII).** The Hypoglossal nerve moves the tongue so you can talk, chew, and swallow — a clean orders-out wire.
